grade.basis: Toccata (Virtuoso, quarter=100) is nonstop chromatic sixteenth runs and leaps in every part for about 19 bars, in canon (PDF pp.1-2); finale bariolage at dotted quarter=150 in 6/8 over string crossings (pp.11-12). Pitch range stays in low positions, so speed and chromatic accuracy set the level.

Limited sample of the full score, so one level of uncertainty.

grade.basis: Complete nine-facing-page parts; inspected all four independent lines, especially pp.2,4,6,8. First violin has nimble dotted dance figures, chromatic semiquavers, grace notes and moderate upper-position work; supporting parts substantially easier. Three is a score-based advisory estimate with one-level uncertainty and no ensemble uplift. Studio-upload whole-work context is plausible but human floor remains unverified.

grade.basis: Violin1 requires upper-register melody, rapid chromatic scale pickups including tuplets, articulate saltellato figures, and repeated high sixteenths at the Finale; lower parts also change between arco and pizzicato and include double stops. The concrete violin1 writing is early advanced rather than a virtuoso concertante part. The factual performance-floor hold is independent of this complete-score advisory grade.

scoreAnchors.location: Ipp1–3, IIpp3–8; II m16/p4 and m32/p4; mm49–64/p5; Finale mm129ff/p8
scoreAnchors.observation: Seven-note and chromatic scale pickups, saltellato bowing, six-note pickups, high repeated sixteenths and closing chords. First movement has sustained pp cantabile/chromatic decoration and staggered entrances.
